summary.business: Cyient DLM is an electronics manufacturing services provider with over three decades of experience, combining engineering expertise with advanced electronics manufacturing — design and prototyping, PCB assembly, cable harness fabrication, box build integration, complex electronics assembly, testing/inspection, supply chain orchestration and aftermarket support — for global and regional OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. It operates a high-mix, low-to-medium volume, high-complexity manufacturing model, and was spun out of Cyient Limited (its holding company), inheriting an engineering co-innovation legacy.

Electronics Manufacturing Services: Interface cards (sound, video, controllers, network, modems)

currentContext.strengths: High-mix, low-to-medium volume, high-complexity manufacturing niche where scale economies break down and technical depth is the competitive advantage, rather than a cost-driven commodity model|Upstream Build-to-Spec engagement — enters at the design stage rather than after design freeze, embedding manufacturability and assuming accountability for field performance, unlike typical build-to-print EMS peers|Breadth of sector-specific certifications (NADCAP, AS9100-D, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, ITAR) forms a qualification barrier to entry that limits competition in regulated sectors|Client roster inherited from Cyient Ltd includes 40% of the world's top 100 innovators|India-US hybrid manufacturing model providing tariff-arbitrage flexibility and a competitive edge amid China+1 sourcing diversification|Long customer qualification cycles and high switching costs once qualified (specifically noted in Med Tech) act as a barrier to entry|33 years of operational legacy / engineering heritage inherited from Cyient Ltd's co-innovation reputation
currentContext.strategies: SET framework — Strengthen, Expand, Transform — anchors execution: strengthening core customer relationships and commercial velocity; expanding into medical, industrial and automotive to reduce defence-cycle concentration; transforming revenue quality by shifting from pure-play manufacturing to end-to-end Build-to-Spec engagements|Strengthen: deepen relationships with core customers and integrate sales, engineering, programme management and operations into a single unit to raise execution discipline and responsiveness|Expand: diversify revenue base across medical, industrial and automotive segments to reduce cyclical dependence on the defence vertical, adding logos with shorter sales/delivery cycles|Transform: move up the value chain into Build-to-Specification (design-led) engagements where the Company contributes engineering value rather than only manufacturing capacity, to protect margins over the long term|Sharpen focus on safety-critical, high-reliability sectors (Aerospace & Defence, Medical Technology) where certification barriers and multi-year qualification cycles limit competition|Invest in capacity ahead of demand, including acquisition of additional land in Mysore to scale operations as customer demand accelerates|Pursue an inorganic growth pipeline targeting acquisitions in Europe and North America, focused on customer proximity and capability enhancement|Continue investing in US operations (India-US hybrid/dual-shore model) to support China+1 sourcing diversification and tariff mitigation for customers|Invest in execution infrastructure — manufacturing systems, automation, digitisation, cable assemblies and LEAN box-build lines — to support consistency at scale and participation in higher-value, design-led programmes
currentContext.expansion: The Company is investing ahead of demand rather than executing a single named capex project: it recently acquired additional land in Mysore to position itself to scale operations as customer demand accelerates, and it is continuing to strengthen its US operations (India-US hybrid manufacturing model) to serve customers amid tariff-driven China+1 supply-chain diversification. Manufacturing capacity utilisation is currently around 50-60%, which management states provides headroom for programme ramps and revenue growth without requiring material additional capital expenditure in the near term. No named capex project with a specific commissioning or completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.note: Middle East conflicts (Gulf/Iranian airspace closures) forced cargo rerouting and inflated freight costs and lead times in H1 FY26; broader geopolitical tensions affect global growth, investment sentiment and supply chain stability. Mitigated via dual-shore (India + USA) manufacturing, contingency logistics/insurance, and a 700+ supplier base spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East and India.

Potential escalation of tariffs on India-origin goods could reduce price competitiveness on shipments to the US and cause customer order deferrals or redirection to non-Indian suppliers, with margin compression if cost increases cannot be passed through. Mitigated via the hybrid India-US manufacturing model and proactive tariff-mitigation options presented to customers.

Revenue volatility from dependence on a few large customers and their programme cycles; a significant revenue impact could follow if a key customer reduces volumes or exits a programme, driving earnings variability tied to programme ramp-up/wind-down. Mitigated by proactive new customer acquisition and vertical diversification into Industrial and Medical Technology to balance Aerospace & Defence exposure.

High import dependence (85-90%) on components creates shortage, cost-inflation and delivery risk, and certain materials/products may become end-of-life or technologically obsolete, risking programme delays and obsolete-stock write-offs. Mitigated via multi-sourcing/second-source qualification, strategic inventory buffers, PLI-supported localisation, and automated obsolescence-detection systems.

Volatility in INR against USD/EUR can erode margins given the mismatch between (largely export) revenue and cost currencies, and cash flow can vary from unhedged FX exposures. Mitigated by natural hedging, selective forward hedging on material exposures and customer price pass-through clauses.

Rapid change in electronics technology requires continuous investment and upgrades; raw materials or finished products can become end-of-life, risking increased capex to keep pace and customer dissatisfaction if obsolescence is not managed proactively. Mitigated by the Design-Led Manufacturing model (reducing reliance on commodity components), ongoing smart-factory investment, and access to Cyient Group's engineering expertise.

Difficulty retaining skilled engineers and technicians in a competitive labour market risks productivity loss, execution delays on complex programmes and loss of institutional knowledge. Mitigated via competitive compensation benchmarking, internal training academies, retention incentives and a Graduate Engineering Trainee programme.

Pressure from larger global and domestic EMS players with scale advantages can exert pricing pressure, compress margins, and risk losing price-sensitive customers. Mitigated by a niche focus on high-reliability, regulated sectors where certification barriers limit competition, and by the Build-to-Specification/Design-Led Manufacturing differentiation.

one-line thesis: The turnaround is now compounding: record-ever order book of INR 2,598 cr (book-to-bill 1.5x), revenue +34.3% YoY, EBITDA +56% and PAT more than doubling, with double-digit EBITDA margin held for a 4th straight quarter. Management reframed the growth story around a phased "Strengthen → Expand → Transform" (SET) roadmap that layers Robotics and AI/Data-Centre onto the proven aerospace/industrial core to walk EBITDA margins from ~9-11% today toward 13-18% by FY30+. Near-term the model is executing cleanly despite West Asia logistics friction; the swing factor remains working-capital (inventory build) and conversion of the record backlog.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 3,738 mn (INR 373.8 cr) | +34.3% | vs INR 2,784 mn Q1FY26; ahead of Q4FY26 too |
| EBITDA / margin | INR 392 mn · 10.5% margin | +56.2% (margin +147 bps) | 4th consecutive double-digit-margin quarter; seq. lower than Q4FY26's INR 431 mn |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | INR 163 mn · 4.4% margin | +118.2% (margin +168 bps) | more than doubled; vs INR 75 mn Q1FY26. PBT INR 222 mn |
| Gross margin | slightly down QoQ | — | mgmt: mix + budgeted org investments; material cost up on B2S procurement |
| Order book | INR 25,989 mn (INR 2,598 cr) | +INR 1,832 mn QoQ | highest ever; from INR 21.3 bn Q1FY26 |
| Cash / net debt | Op cash flow still negative; finance cost −29% YoY | — | driven by inventory build + lower customer advances |
> One-offs / distortions: forex hit on the balance sheet from ~1 month of rupee appreciation (net exporter). Gross margin dipped sequentially on business mix + deliberate, pre-budgeted investment in the commercial organisation (new leadership hires), not a demand problem.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** No hard number given; "similar momentum" in revenue/order-intake range expected in Q2 and through FY27; CFO pointed analysts to "aspirational revenue growth rates" combined with the 1.5x book-to-bill (i.e. compute it).
- **Margin:** "Expand" phase (FY27-FY29) EBITDA margin **11-13%**; "Transform" phase (FY30+) **13-18%**. Core stack runs ~9-11% today. B2S adds **+250-300 bps** to consolidated EBITDA margin as it scales.
- **Order book / inflow target:** Book-to-bill **~1.5x maintained for the full year** FY27 (declined to give an absolute year-end order-book number).
- **Capex / commissioning:** No major expansion capex — only regular annual maintenance capex; existing installed capacity can support ~1.75-2x current revenue and new AI/robotics lanes need no additional capex.
order book & pipeline:
- Record order book **INR 2,598 cr**; order intake **INR 551.9 cr** in the quarter (no lumpy one-off — broad-based across existing + new customers), book-to-bill **1.5x**.
- ~70% of intake from existing customers, ~30% from logos added in the last 4-6 quarters; management stresses "a lot of opportunity still" with existing accounts.
- Sales pipeline described as "substantially higher" than order book (well above the ~USD 0.5 bn / INR 4,000-5,000 cr an analyst floated) — not disclosed. Pipeline mix ≈ 48% aerospace & defence, <40% industrial/semiconductor cap-equipment, balance medical + small auto.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Industry mix:** Aerospace 42% (+40% YoY), Industrial 32% (+90% YoY), Defence 9% (+35% YoY), MedTech 16% (flat YoY — seasonal softness at one customer), Auto/others 1%.
- **Product mix:** PCBA 48% (+21% YoY), Box Build 41% (+85% YoY), Mechanical/others 10% (incl. B2S), Cables 1%.
  <!-- corrected 2026-08-04: Box Build was recorded as 21%, contaminated by PCBA's 21% YoY growth rate
       one sentence earlier in the transcript. The deck states 41%, and the mix only sums to 100% at 41%. -->
- **Geography:** Rest-of-World 94%, India 6% (RoW led by aerospace/medical/defence/industrial customers outside India).
- **Altek (US, ITAR-certified):** one defence project live, engaging more US defence customers — early pipeline; potential North America defence-tech route.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **SET roadmap:** Strengthen (today, 4 industries, ~9-11% margin) → Expand (FY27-29, add Robotics + AI/Data-Centre = 6 industries, 11-13%) → Transform (FY30+, own B2S products/IP, 13-18%).
- **B2S:** lab doubled 6,000 → 15,000 sq ft; strong order pipeline; meaningful revenue in the next 12-18 months; a Japan eVTOL/EAV customer (SkyDrive-type) in engineering-design stage, ~12-18 months to production, then whole-lifecycle build.
- **AI/Data-Centre & Robotics:** sales directors on board this quarter; order intake expected in FY27, revenue later; specific product lines (power supply/cooling/compute hardware) to be disclosed in 2-3 quarters; deliverable with existing capabilities.
- **Semiconductor cap-equipment:** building products for existing customers; revenue growth over next 6-12 months.
- **Honeywell Aerospace + Thales:** early builds of large multi-year wins now ramping — "extraordinary growth this year" and over the next 18 months.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Aerospace qualification moat (explicitly evidenced):** CFO — "The aerospace business is a double-edged sword. It's very, very difficult to get into. But once you are in you're in… that's a moat that's impossible to reach for a new entrant, and we're in the moat." Company is qualified with "every single major OEM or significant Tier-1 that buys any electronics" (Honeywell, Thales, Safran, BAE, etc.).
- **Certifications as barrier:** completed Nadcap audit (demanding aerospace-grade) for cable-harness at Mysore; ITAR-certified Altek unit — regulatory/qualification barriers that reinforce high-reliability positioning.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Normalized EBITDA margin 10.5% (+147 bps YoY from 9.0%); operating leverage + better revenue mix + disciplined cost the drivers ("filling the hopper").
- Sequential gross-margin dip from mix + pre-budgeted investment in commercial org; not structural.
- Finance costs −29% YoY on lower working-capital borrowings. Future margin step-up mapped to new higher-value lanes + B2S (+250-300 bps) rather than pure cost-out.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Capital-light: B2S lab doubled to 15,000 sq ft is the notable capacity add; no major expansion capex planned. Existing plant can support ~1.75-2x current revenue; AI/robotics/semicon lanes executable on existing machinery + selective application-engineering hires.
capital allocation: - Reinvesting into working capital (inventory as a "leading indicator" to protect deliveries through West Asia disruption) and into commercial-org build-out. No buyback/dividend signalled; disciplined, growth-stage EMS. IPO-proceeds utilisation continuing (from prior quarters).
risks & watch-items:
- **Working capital / negative operating cash flow:** inventory build (DIO 162 days vs 153 QoQ) + lower customer advances (15 vs 18 days); NWC 161 days (vs 145). Mgmt expects cash flow to turn positive once growth-inventory normalises.
- **West Asia / geopolitics:** logistics delays and higher shipping cost; mitigated by strategic inventory and alternate sourcing — no Q1 impact, planning to shield Q2, but ongoing.
- **Forex:** large two-way (export + import) exposure → balance-sheet swings on rupee moves.
- **Customer concentration / lumpiness** in aerospace-defence; MedTech seasonally soft; new AI/data-centre lane is early and unproven with no disclosed products yet.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Chairman Bodanapu credited CEO Velagapudi with the turnaround. Transparent on what they won't guide (absolute order-book, segment-wise new-lane %), consistent messaging on the SET roadmap. CFO candid ("aerospace is always an investment for the first few years"). No over-promising on AI/data-centre — repeatedly deferred specifics 2-3 quarters.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Book-to-bill held at 1.5x *for the full year* is effectively a soft growth signal — pair with "aspirational" growth rates and the record backlog to back into strong FY27 revenue.
- The AI/data-centre entry is deliberately capability-first, capex-light and unguided — optionality, not yet a numbers story; management flagged data-centre demand is inherently cyclical ("it's up now, it will go down") vs aerospace as the steady base.
- Industrial +90% YoY and Box-Build +85% YoY are the quarter's real engines, not aerospace alone — diversification is working.
- Margin ladder (9-11 → 11-13 → 13-18%) is explicitly product/lane-mix driven (B2S + new industries), giving a multi-year re-rating framework to verify against.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cyient DLM is an electronics manufacturing services provider with over three decades of experience, combining engineering expertise with advanced electronics manufacturing — design and prototyping, PCB assembly, cable harness fabrication, box build integration, complex electronics assembly, testing/inspection, supply chain orchestration and aftermarket support — for global and regional OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. It operates a high-mix, low-to-medium volume, high-complexity manufacturing model, and was spun out of Cyient Limited (its holding company), inheriting an engineering co-innovation legacy.

group_structure.body:
- Cyient DLM Inc. (USA) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); provides Electronics Manufacturing Services under intercompany agreements with the holding/fellow subsidiaries
- Altek Electronics Inc. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (100%), effective October 4, 2024 — established the Company's North America presence
- Cyient Limited — related party: Holding company (52% shareholding); electronics manufacturing services provided under intercompany/tripartite agreements
- Cyient Inc. — related party: Fellow subsidiary
- Cyient GmbH — related party: Fellow subsidiary

- Cyient K.K — related party: Fellow subsidiary

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Industry mix:** Aerospace 42% (+40% YoY), Industrial 32% (+90% YoY), Defence 9% (+35% YoY), MedTech 16% (flat YoY — seasonal softness at one customer), Auto/others 1%.
- **Product mix:** PCBA 48% (+21% YoY), Box Build 41% (+85% YoY), Mechanical/others 10% (incl. B2S), Cables 1%.

- **Geography:** Rest-of-World 94%, India 6% (RoW led by aerospace/medical/defence/industrial customers outside India).
- **Altek (US, ITAR-certified):** one defence project live, engaging more US defence customers — early pipeline; potential North America defence-tech route.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Record order book **INR 2,598 cr**; order intake **INR 551.9 cr** in the quarter (no lumpy one-off — broad-based across existing + new customers), book-to-bill **1.5x**.
- ~70% of intake from existing customers, ~30% from logos added in the last 4-6 quarters; management stresses "a lot of opportunity still" with existing accounts.
- Sales pipeline described as "substantially higher" than order book (well above the ~USD 0.5 bn / INR 4,000-5,000 cr an analyst floated) — not disclosed. Pipeline mix ≈ 48% aerospace & defence, <40% industrial/semiconductor cap-equipment, balance medical + small auto.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** No hard number given; "similar momentum" in revenue/order-intake range expected in Q2 and through FY27; CFO pointed analysts to "aspirational revenue growth rates" combined with the 1.5x book-to-bill (i.e. compute it).
- **Margin:** "Expand" phase (FY27-FY29) EBITDA margin **11-13%**; "Transform" phase (FY30+) **13-18%**. Core stack runs ~9-11% today. B2S adds **+250-300 bps** to consolidated EBITDA margin as it scales.
- **Order book / inflow target:** Book-to-bill **~1.5x maintained for the full year** FY27 (declined to give an absolute year-end order-book number).
- **Capex / commissioning:** No major expansion capex — only regular annual maintenance capex; existing installed capacity can support ~1.75-2x current revenue and new AI/robotics lanes need no additional capex.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **SET roadmap:** Strengthen (today, 4 industries, ~9-11% margin) → Expand (FY27-29, add Robotics + AI/Data-Centre = 6 industries, 11-13%) → Transform (FY30+, own B2S products/IP, 13-18%).
- **B2S:** lab doubled 6,000 → 15,000 sq ft; strong order pipeline; meaningful revenue in the next 12-18 months; a Japan eVTOL/EAV customer (SkyDrive-type) in engineering-design stage, ~12-18 months to production, then whole-lifecycle build.
- **AI/Data-Centre & Robotics:** sales directors on board this quarter; order intake expected in FY27, revenue later; specific product lines (power supply/cooling/compute hardware) to be disclosed in 2-3 quarters; deliverable with existing capabilities.
- **Semiconductor cap-equipment:** building products for existing customers; revenue growth over next 6-12 months.
- **Honeywell Aerospace + Thales:** early builds of large multi-year wins now ramping — "extraordinary growth this year" and over the next 18 months.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AI infrastructure build-out is expanding electronics content per system, a direct tailwind for high-complexity PCBA and Box Build demand
- Defence budget expansion (EU's €800bn ReArm Europe initiative, US and India MoD modernisation toward electronic warfare, autonomous platforms and next-generation combat systems) is driving Aerospace & Defence electronics demand
- China+1 diversification is directing OEM sourcing toward India; the Company's India-US hybrid model and structured tariff migration framework are cited as a key strength that helped win new logos across industries
- INR depreciation improves export competitiveness for the Company's USD- and EUR-denominated revenues, which account for the majority of consolidated top line
- Operating leverage: as revenues grow, fixed manufacturing costs are absorbed more efficiently
- Capacity headroom, with utilisation currently at approximately 50-60%, provides runway for programme ramps without additional capital investment
- Rising contribution from design-led (Build-to-Spec) programmes, which carry higher margins and lower commoditisation risk
- India's EMS sector is described as entering a 'decisive decade' — exports projected to triple by 2030 and India's global EMS market share expected to rise from ~4% toward 7%+ by decade end
- Industrial vertical (~30% of consolidated revenue) provides a more balanced portfolio versus prior Aerospace & Defence concentration; Altek's US industrial operations delivered 425% YoY revenue growth
- Med Tech (~15% of consolidated revenue) is structurally resistant to margin compression given compliance-driven, high-reliability nature; Altek's US med-tech revenue grew 142% YoY
- Automotive remains a high-growth diversification segment supported by EV/ADAS-driven electronics complexity; an EV charging infrastructure order was won from an India-based, globally-backed client
- Balance sheet remains strong with a net cash position and net working capital of 145 days, providing flexibility to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline
- Book-to-bill ratio above 1 sustained in every quarter of FY26, closing the year at 1.46x (MD-CEO letter) / 1.5x (MD&A outlook)
- Order intake for FY26 was H18,430 mn, representing over 90% year-on-year growth
- Order backlog at year-end FY26 reached H24,166 mn — the highest level in over two years — providing strong visibility into FY27 revenue
- Pipeline described as robust with improving conversion across key segments entering FY27

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Normalized EBITDA margin 10.5% (+147 bps YoY from 9.0%); operating leverage + better revenue mix + disciplined cost the drivers ("filling the hopper").
- Sequential gross-margin dip from mix + pre-budgeted investment in commercial org; not structural.
- Finance costs −29% YoY on lower working-capital borrowings. Future margin step-up mapped to new higher-value lanes + B2S (+250-300 bps) rather than pure cost-out.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Reinvesting into working capital (inventory as a "leading indicator" to protect deliveries through West Asia disruption) and into commercial-org build-out. No buyback/dividend signalled; disciplined, growth-stage EMS. IPO-proceeds utilisation continuing (from prior quarters).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is investing ahead of demand rather than executing a single named capex project: it recently acquired additional land in Mysore to position itself to scale operations as customer demand accelerates, and it is continuing to strengthen its US operations (India-US hybrid manufacturing model) to serve customers amid tariff-driven China+1 supply-chain diversification. Manufacturing capacity utilisation is currently around 50-60%, which management states provides headroom for programme ramps and revenue growth without requiring material additional capital expenditure in the near term. No named capex project with a specific commissioning or completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and execution-focused; Chairman Bodanapu credited CEO Velagapudi with the turnaround. Transparent on what they won't guide (absolute order-book, segment-wise new-lane %), consistent messaging on the SET roadmap. CFO candid ("aerospace is always an investment for the first few years"). No over-promising on AI/data-centre — repeatedly deferred specifics 2-3 quarters.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- High-mix, low-to-medium volume, high-complexity manufacturing niche where scale economies break down and technical depth is the competitive advantage, rather than a cost-driven commodity model
- Upstream Build-to-Spec engagement — enters at the design stage rather than after design freeze, embedding manufacturability and assuming accountability for field performance, unlike typical build-to-print EMS peers
- Breadth of sector-specific certifications (NADCAP, AS9100-D, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, ITAR) forms a qualification barrier to entry that limits competition in regulated sectors
- Client roster inherited from Cyient Ltd includes 40% of the world's top 100 innovators
- India-US hybrid manufacturing model providing tariff-arbitrage flexibility and a competitive edge amid China+1 sourcing diversification
- Long customer qualification cycles and high switching costs once qualified (specifically noted in Med Tech) act as a barrier to entry
- 33 years of operational legacy / engineering heritage inherited from Cyient Ltd's co-innovation reputation

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Working capital / negative operating cash flow:** inventory build (DIO 162 days vs 153 QoQ) + lower customer advances (15 vs 18 days); NWC 161 days (vs 145). Mgmt expects cash flow to turn positive once growth-inventory normalises.
- **West Asia / geopolitics:** logistics delays and higher shipping cost; mitigated by strategic inventory and alternate sourcing — no Q1 impact, planning to shield Q2, but ongoing.
- **Forex:** large two-way (export + import) exposure → balance-sheet swings on rupee moves.
- **Customer concentration / lumpiness** in aerospace-defence; MedTech seasonally soft; new AI/data-centre lane is early and unproven with no disclosed products yet.
